newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Euro-handover gesture falls flat.
newsitem.headline: French Euro-handover gesture falls flat.

text.p: It was meant to be an ecumenical gesture of European unity but it fell flat.

France's outgoing Gaullist European affairs minister, Michel Barnier, presented his Socialist successor, Pierre Moscovici, with a photograph of general Charles de Gaulle shaking hands in reconciliation with postwar German chancellor Konrad Adenauer.
"I am giving you this because it symbolises the reason for my involvement in public life," an emotional Barnier said at their handover ceremony at the foreign ministry on Thursday.
"I am leaving it with him because it's not necessarily the reason for my political commitment," Moscovici replied.
There was a moment's silence. Had the new minister really refused the gift?
Barnier insisted: "I leave it to him."
Moscovici then took the picture and said: "It will be in a good place, but there may be others because they were not the only founding fathers of Europe."
The terse exchange symbolised the tension between the defeated centre-right coalition and the victorious left-wing alliance over European policy.

Barnier, who was France's chief negotiator at the European Union's intergovernmental conference on institutional reform, was given a farewell gift of a map of 17th century Europe by his 14 EU colleagues at a farewell meeting in Brussels earlier on Thursday.
He said the hardest part of the reform, changing the weighted majority voting system to make decision-making easier and more equitable, was still uncertain.
"I hope they won't give in to the temptation to postpone real institutional reform until later, because this really is the last chance for a long time," Barnier told Reuters.

Officials said Moscovici, a member of the European parliament, would not replace Barnier at the talks, which are nearing competion with an EU summit in Amsterdam on June 16-17. France would be represented instead by its EU ambassador.
